Tracking Interaction in YouTube and Vimeo iFrame APIs

Interact with the videos below and watch the data update. The behavior for both players is very similar, with a few discrepancies as to when different events fire (see below).

In the data, sequence is a history of the interaction with completed percentages when the event was triggered. furthest is the highest percentage of completion achieved in the interaction. stops is a count of the amount of times the video complete event fired. These metrics should be enough to derive an accurate picture of how the interaction unfolded; however, they are dependent on the pause, play, and stop events. If you were to navigate from the page while the video is playing, progress would not be updated.

This Vimeo approach uses their suggested froogaloop plugin. Vimeo API Documentation can be found on developer.vimeo.com. YouTube's documentation can be found on developers.google.com. Oh, and Ratatat is amazing.


  


  

    
    

  








  

    
Discrepancies

    
    
      
  • Vimeo player indicates the stop event and play event after stop are at 100.2%.
    •  
      
  • YouTube player indicates stop is at 100% and play after stop is at 0%. 
      
  • Vimeo player fires two stop events on finish.
    • 
      
  • YouTube player fires an additional play event if you skip ahead past the buffer.
    •  
      
  • YouTube player fires an additional pause event when skipping ahead while paused.
